facts.statement: Zhengheornis fossils were discovered in March to April 2024 near Yangyuan Village in Zhenghe County, Fujian Province, China.
facts.quote: The Zhengheornis fossil material was discovered during fieldwork from March to April 2024, in outcrops of the Nanyuan Formation ('layer 6') near Yangyuan Village of Zhenghe County, Fujian Province, China.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Zhengheornis is housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology under the accession number IVPP V34168.
facts.quote: The specimen is housed in the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology (IVPP), where it is permanently accessioned as specimen IVPP V34168.

facts.statement: Zhengheornis lived during the Late Jurassic, specifically the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian ages, in China.
facts.quote: Zhengheornis () is an extinct genus of basal avialan known from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian–Tithonian ages) Nanyuan Formation of China.

facts.statement: Zhengheornis lived approximately 150 million years ago at the boundary between the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Zhengheornis is known from the Nanyuan Formation, which dates to around 150 million years ago, around the border between the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian ages of the late Jurassic period.

facts.statement: The time range for Zhengheornis is estimated from 152.21 to 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 145.06 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Nanyuan Formation, where Zhengheornis was found, represents a primarily swamp-like environment.
facts.quote: The outcrops of this formation have been interpreted as representing a primarily swamp-like depositional environment.

facts.statement: Zhengheornis is classified as an early member of the Avialae, with Z. buyu as its type species.
facts.quote: Notes: An early member of Avialae. The type species is Z. buyu.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Zhengheornis within Avialae, diverging after Anchiornithidae and Archaeopteryx but before Baminornis.
facts.quote: Zhengheornis was recovered as a member of the Avialae, diverging after Anchiornithidae and Archaeopteryx, but immediately before the coeval Baminornis.

facts.statement: Research suggests Zhengheornis and Yuezhuornis form a sister-taxon clade named Zhengheornithidae.
facts.quote: Using the matrix of Wang et al., they recovered Yuezhuornis and Zhengheornis as sister taxa, a clade they named Zhengheornithidae.

facts.statement: Zhengheornis provides evidence that vertebral reduction and shortening occurred before pygostyle fusion in the stepwise evolution of the bird tail.
The exact position of Zhengheornis relative to Anchiornithidae, Archaeopteryx, and Baminornis is a subject of phylogenetic reconstruction.
facts.quote: Zhengheornis was recovered as a member of the Avialae, diverging after Anchiornithidae and Archaeopteryx, but immediately before the coeval Baminornis.
